title: Throughput spectrometer: tokens/sec microprobe for core models
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build and maintain a tokens-per-second microbenchmark 'spectrometer' that profiles core serving models across realistic sequence lengths, prefix distributions, and KV-cache warmup states, with p95 tail tracking and automated regression detection. The harness must run fast (minutes per commit), be stable across stochastic seeds, and surface clear signal for kernel/quantization and routing changes.

Scope and requirements:
- Core models: rdx-small, rdx-medium, rdx-large (and LTS variants).
- Measurements: steady-state tokens/sec, cold-start vs warmed KV cache, p50/p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, memory and host-side jitter.
- Workloads: short-chat (avg 32 tokens), assistant-long (avg 512 tokens), embedding-like (single long-infer), and microburst (many short parallel requests).
- Regression detection: daily baselines, rolling 14-day window, alerts when tokens/sec drops >7% at p95 or p50 falls below SLA. Alerts should produce a triage card with recent diffs and flamegraphs.
- CI: lightweight nightly and GH-PR checks (fast smoke). Full sweep runs on khan-giant-worker pool.
- Outputs: numeric artifacts (CSV/JSON), per-model performance profiles stored in S3 (versioned by model+commit), dashboard panels in Grafana, and failing-commit traces attached to Linear ticket.

High level approach:
1) Reuse and extend existing microbench harness (ENG-5931 style) but swap to deterministic workload generator and add KV-warmup state machines.
2) Implement adaptive sampling to keep run-time bounded: quick exploratory warm runs then focused longer measurement for noisy configs.
3) Integrate Prometheus exporters and push metrics for p95 tokens/sec to the central metrics pipeline. Add a separate regression detector service that runs nightly comparing baseline artifacts.
4) Add lightweight ML-driven anomaly filter to reduce false positives caused by cluster maintenance windows.

Deliverables and acceptance criteria:
- Runnable harness with documented CLI and docker image (redwood/throughput-spectrometer:canary).
- CI job that runs on PRs (10–20s smoke) and nightly full sweep (45–90m depending on model set).
- Grafana dashboard with historical tokens/sec, p95 bands, and alerting rules wired into Opsgenie.
- Regression detector that files a Linear ticket automatically with attached diff reports and trace links when triggered.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Running full sweeps on core models consumes significant GPU hours; mitigate by sampling and reserving dedicated burst pool for night runs.
- Determinism vs realism: overly deterministic inputs hide real-world variance; we'll keep a seeded random generator and expose an 'operational variability' knob.
- Alert noise: initial thresholds may cause churn; we'll tune thresholds after one month on canary.

- Performance primer slides: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X-throughput-spectrometer-primer

Operational notes:
- Nightly runs will tag artifacts with tree commit SHA and model revision; an automated small snapshot will be kept for 30 days, full artifacts for 90 days.
- Integration with Console: expose per-route tokens/sec deltas as a 'regression insight' card via the console-telemetry ingestion path.

Next steps (short term):
- M1: Merge harness skeleton and dockerfile (owner: Miguel) — 3d.
- M2: Add KV-warmup state machine and stable workload generator (owner: Priya Rao) — 5d.
- M3: Hook Prometheus metrics + build Grafana dashboard (owner: Dev Ops) — 4d.
- M4: Nightly regression detector + autopost ticketing (owner: Aisha) — 6d.
